edges.interpretation: The proposed opcode makes x-only key tweak addition available inside script.

evidence.excerpt: The opcode accepts a raw 32-byte scalar instead of internally hashing the input or computing a Taproot-specific tweak. This keeps the consensus rule minimal. Constructions that require a hashed tweak can apply `OP_SHA256` before `OP_TWEAKADD`. Constructions that require a BIP341 tweak to be computed entirely on-chain would require additional general-purpose opcodes that expose tapleaf hashes or taptree commitments to script.
